records.d: Humans have burned incense to release controlled scent for over 5,000 years: temples, homes, and ceremonies scented on purpose. The oldest form of the smell-generating device is a censer. Every digital scent cartridge descends from burning resin for atmosphere.
records.h: Resins and woods combusted to release aromatic compounds into the air, with the burner controlling timing and intensity. Scent was scheduled. The censer was the first programmable scent device, programmed by hand.
k: The censer as first scent device
records.mj: Established - documented ancient incense use; controlled scent release.
records.t: c. 3000 BCE: Incense - Controlled Scent Begins
records.z: timeline|year=-3000|span=1|events=incense burning in rituals~first controlled scent release

records.d: By around 1000 CE, distillation produced concentrated perfumes: scent captured, bottled, and released on demand. The perfume bottle was a scent storage device. Captured scent became portable.
records.h: Steam distillation separated aromatic oils from plant material, concentrating scent into portable liquids. The bottle stored the experience. Scent became a product you could carry.
records.mj: Established - documented distillation of perfumes; portable scent.
records.t: c. 1000 CE: Distilled Perfume - Scent in a Bottle

records.d: In 1874, chemists synthesized vanillin, the main aroma compound of vanilla: scent made from chemistry, not crops. Synthetic aroma compounds made any smell manufacturable. The scent palette became infinite.
records.h: Organic synthesis built vanillin molecules identical to the natural compound, freeing flavor and fragrance from agriculture. Factories could print scent. The chemical palette underlies every modern scent device.
records.mj: Established - documented 1874 vanillin synthesis; synthetic aroma compounds.

records.d: AromaRama debuted in 1959 with 'Behind the Great Wall,' pumping scents through theater air conditioning synced to the film. Cinema's first scent track. The audience could smell the movie.
records.h: Theater ventilation systems released fragrances on cue from the projection booth during key scenes. Thirty-plus scents played. The theater became a scent device, though the smells lingered and mixed.
records.mj: Established - documented 1959 AromaRama debut; scented cinema.

records.d: Smell-O-Vision launched in 1960 with 'Scent of Mystery,' delivering 30 odors to individual theater seats through pipes. Personal scent delivery at the movies. The seat became the scent device.
records.h: Each seat had tubes connected to scent reservoirs, releasing puffs on cue. The system was installed for one film and removed. Personal delivery solved the mixing problem but not the cost one.
records.mj: Established - documented 1960 Smell-O-Vision; piped seat-level scent.

records.d: Scratch-and-sniff, popularized in the 1980s on stickers and books, stored scent in microcapsules released by scratching. Scent on demand, at pocket scale. Millions of children operated scent devices with their fingernails.
records.h: Microencapsulated fragrance oils embedded in coatings broke open under friction, releasing scent. The interface was a fingernail. Disposable, cheap, and everywhere, it proved consumers loved on-demand smell.
records.mj: Established - documented 1980s scratch-n-sniff; microencapsulated scent.

records.d: DigiScents unveiled the iSmell in 1999: a USB peripheral that would emit scents for websites and games from cartridges. The first digital scent device for PCs. It raised tens of millions, then died in the dot-com crash: right idea, wrong decade.
records.h: The shark-fin device held a cartridge of scented oils, releasing puffs keyed to web content and games via a plugin. No content ecosystem materialized. The hardware waited for software that never came.
records.mj: Established - documented 1999 DigiScents iSmell; USB scent peripheral.

records.d: TriSenx's Scent Dome, shown around 2002, was a desktop dome that released scents for games and DVDs from 20 cartridges. The PC scent peripheral tried again. Like iSmell, it waited for content that never arrived.
records.h: Twenty scent cartridges mixed puffs under software control while the user sat in the dome's airflow. Demos impressed; sales didn't. The lesson repeated: scent hardware needs a content standard.
records.mj: Established - documented TriSenx Scent Dome; desktop scent peripheral.

records.d: In the 2000s, NTT researched 'fragrance communication': networked scent delivery for messaging and presence. Scent as a communications medium. The phone call you could smell was a research program.
records.h: Networked scent devices synchronized aroma release with messages and calls in lab trials. Presence gained a channel. The research framed smell as information, not just atmosphere.
records.mj: Established - documented NTT fragrance-communication research; networked scent.
records.z: timeline|year=2005|span=1|events=NTT fragrance communication research~scent as a medium

c: Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology, 2011
records.d: In 2011, researchers built the Smelling Screen: an LCD with corner fans wafting scents so the smell seemed to come from the screen image. The display gained a nose. Digital scent met the screen.
records.h: Scent cartridges behind the display released puffs through fans aimed to create a localized scent field matching on-screen objects. The illusion placed smell in the image. The screen became multisensory.
k: Scents seeming to come from the image
records.mj: Established - documented 2011 Smelling Screen; screen-localized scent.

records.d: Scentee, launched in 2013 by ChatPerf, was a smartphone accessory that puffed scents for messages and games from a replaceable tank. The phone gained a nose. Mobile made scent personal.
records.h: A phone-attached module vaporized scented liquid on app command, synced to notifications and content. The tank refilled the experience. The smartphone, the most personal device, became a scent device.
records.mj: Established - documented 2013 Scentee launch; smartphone scent accessory.
records.t: 2013: Scentee - the Phone Gets a Nose

records.d: The oPhone, from Harvard's David Edwards and shown in 2014, composed 'scent messages' from 32 base aromas: texting in smell. A new medium was proposed. The oPhone treated scent as a language with an alphabet.
records.h: Thirty-two base scent chips combined into thousands of 'oNotes' sent between devices. The composition was the message. Treating smell as composable made it a communications medium.
records.mj: Established - documented 2014 oPhone; composable scent messaging.

records.d: Feelreal's VR mask, crowdfunded in 2015, added smell, wind, heat, and mist to virtual reality: the face became the interface. VR's missing sense got hardware. Immersion went multisensory.
records.h: The mask held replaceable scent cartridges plus heaters, coolers, and misters, triggered by game events. The face wore the weather. Multisensory VR became a purchasable upgrade.
k: VR mask with smell, wind, heat
records.mj: Established - documented 2015 Feelreal campaign; multisensory VR mask.

records.d: VAQSO, launched in 2017, made a VR scent attachment with swappable cartridges for games and arcades. Scent joined the VR arcade stack. Location-based VR became smellable.
records.h: A clip-on module released scent puffs synced to VR scenes, with cartridges swapped per experience. Arcades adopted it for immersion. The attachment model fit VR's accessory market.
records.mj: Emerging - real shipped product; VR scent attachment for games and arcades.

records.d: OVR Technology's ION, shown in 2019, was a wearable scent device for VR/AR with software-timed release. Scent became a developer API. The nose joined the SDK.
records.h: The wearable held scent cartridges released on software triggers, with an SDK for experience designers. Developers scripted smell like sound. Scent became a design material.
records.mj: Emerging - real product and SDK; software-timed wearable scent.
records.t: 2019: OVR ION - Scent as an API

records.d: Aromajoin's Aroma Shooter, shipping around 2020, was a wearable that fired directional scent shots synced to media. Smell gained aim. The wearable scent shooter made digital aroma directional.
records.h: A neck-worn device shot scented air toward the nose on cue, with cartridges for different experiences. Direction replaced diffusion. Wearable, personal, and precise.
records.mj: Established - documented Aromajoin wearable; directional scent delivery.

records.d: Smell training, widely adopted around 2020 for post-viral anosmia, had patients sniff sets of strong scents daily to rebuild olfactory function: scent as medicine. The nose could be rehabilitated. Digital scent found a clinical use.
records.h: Repeated structured exposure to distinct odorants stimulated olfactory recovery, with kits standardizing the protocol. Therapy was low-tech but evidence-backed. Scent delivery became healthcare.
records.mj: Established - documented clinical practice; smell training for anosmia rehabilitation.

records.d: By 2021, VR training simulations were adding scent cues: smoke for firefighter drills, chemicals for hazmat practice. Smell made training serious. The nose joined the simulator.
records.h: Scent devices released context-matched odors during training scenarios, reinforcing memory and stress inoculation. The cue was cheap; the realism gain was large. Olfaction proved its training value.
records.mj: Emerging - real training deployments; scented VR for hazard training.

records.d: By 2022, scent cartridges were standardizing across devices: replaceable, swappable, increasingly cross-compatible. The razor-and-blades model reached smell. The consumable made the hardware business work.
records.h: Manufacturers converged on cartridge formats with defined scent loads and lifespans. The consumable economics funded hardware. Standardization, even partial, grew the market.
records.mj: Emerging - real market development; standardizing scent cartridges.

records.d: Osmo, spun out of Google research in 2023, set out to digitize scent: AI predicting smells from molecular structure, building a map of odor. Smell became computable. The nose got a digital twin.
records.h: Machine-learning models trained on molecular data predicted odor character, aiming for a general scent model. Digitization promised scent telegraphy. Olfaction joined vision and hearing as modelable senses.
records.mj: Emerging - real company and research (2023); AI scent digitization.
records.z: timeline|year=2023|span=1|events=Osmo spins out of Google~AI maps odor

records.d: By 2023, AI was designing commercial fragrances: models proposing novel scent combinations that perfumers refined. The perfumer gained an AI apprentice. Creation, not just delivery, went digital.
records.h: Generative models trained on fragrance formulas proposed novel combinations, with human perfumers evaluating and refining. The AI explored; the nose decided. Design joined delivery in the digital scent stack.
records.mj: Emerging - real industry practice; AI-designed fragrances.

records.d: By 2024, theme parks and location-based VR were deploying scent as standard immersion: ocean air, gunpowder, bakeries on cue. Smell became show design. The attraction had a scent script.
records.h: Facility-scale scent systems released timed fragrances through venues synced to rides and shows. The scent script joined the show script. Out-of-home entertainment led adoption.
records.mj: Emerging - real deployments; facility-scale scented entertainment.

records.d: By 2025, consumer VR scent add-ons were maturing: lighter wearables, longer cartridges, game-native support. The nose was becoming standard VR equipment. Multisensory VR was leaving the arcade.
records.h: Improved miniaturization and battery life made scent wearables practical for home VR, with engines adding scent events. The accessory became expected. Home immersion caught up.
records.mj: Emerging - real maturing products; consumer VR scent wearables.
